RedPine is completing a SIG/CAIQ review for our Q4 procurement cycle and we need a compact artefact describing Redwood's vulnerability management posture focused on scan cadence, remediation SLAs, and a short attestation we can include in our security binder. - Scan cadence (image / dependency / network) and who owns the schedule

- Evidence of recent scans (last 90 days) and high-level results

On Tue, Sep 5, 2028 at 12:03 PM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Appreciate the context and timeline. We'll assemble a compact packet and a concise attestation paragraph.

Hi Liam / Aditya —

Attached are the two artifacts: (1) slo_matrix.xlsx — VM cadence and remediation SLAs, and (2) vm_scan_summary_Q3.pdf — consolidated high-level scan results (non-sensitive summary). Highlights:

- Scan cadence: image scanning (weekly), dependency SCA (daily for critical repos + daily snapshot for mirrors), network vulnerability scans (bi-weekly internal, monthly external).
- Remediation SLAs (target):
  - P1 (critical / RCE / privilege escalation): 7 days to fix or documented compensating control + 24-48hr mitigation plan
  - P2 (high): 30 days to remediation or documented exception with compensating controls
  - P3 (medium/low): 90 days standard cadence; prioritization based on exploitability score
- Exceptions: formal exception requests routed to InfoSec with documented mitigation and automatic 30/60/90 day review until closure.
- Evidence: summary includes counts and a redacted sample of findings (no sensitive customer data). Full raw scan exports are available under NDA or via secure share.

Formal attestation (text below) — you can paste this into your SIG binder or we can produce a letterhead PDF if you prefer: 

"Redwood Inference maintains an operational vulnerability management program that combines continuous dependency scanning, weekly image scans, and periodic network scanning. Critical vulnerabilities are triaged immediately with a target remediation SLA of 7 calendar days; high severity issues are remediated within 30 days, and medium/low issues follow a 90-day remediation cadence unless greater risk is identified. Exceptions are managed through InfoSec with documented compensating controls and time-boxed reviews. Scan data and remediation records are retained according to our retention policy and are available for audit under appropriate governance controls."

I'm attaching the files referenced. Monica — FYI on retention window (we keep raw exports for 12 months, summaries for 3 years).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
